title: Enforce RBAC and audit trail for Admin actor management

spec.problem: M6 Admin actor and role management accepts any active Admin session and creates/changes access without permission checks or durable audit events.

acceptance.text: An Admin without iam.manage receives 403 on actor/role management reads and writes; an Admin with iam.manage retains the documented API contracts.

Successful actor create, status change, role grant and role revoke write ops.admin_audit_log records with action, authenticated actor, target identity and safe before/after snapshots; password material is never recorded.

GET /api/admin/ads/audit enforces ads.audit.view, admin.monetization.read, or viewer.audit in the Go backend; an Admin session without any accepted permission gets 403 while a least-privilege audit viewer succeeds.
The Admin account management route renders an Admin list item returned by the current Go API contract (role codes in roles[]) without a page error and displays the assigned roles.
POST /api/admin/ads/rules accepts a valid disposable rule, persists it and returns HTTP 200 with its id, ruleKey and enabled state; subsequent GET includes the rule.

Every /api/admin/ads endpoint enforces its domain permission in the Go backend: campaign reads require admin.monetization.read or ads.campaign.view, campaign mutations require admin.monetization.write or ads.campaign.manage, and frontend route hiding cannot grant access.

Admin analytics export summary, timeseries, and breakdown views contain values derived from their real analytics handlers; an empty period reports genuine empty/zero data rather than a placeholder, and unsupported views return 400.

Admin analytics executive and domain read/export endpoints require viewer.analytics, admin.analytics.view, or analytics.view at the backend; export and refresh mutations also accept admin.analytics.manage.

spec.expected_behavior: Require iam.manage for actor and role management; persist auditable before/after events for successful mutations without logging credentials.
spec.observed_behavior: The Ads client hides the Audit tab by permission but loads the audit endpoint for every Admin session; the Go route is registered under AdminGuard only.

classification.rationale: Enforce backend RBAC and transactional audit for Admin actor management; refresh the SQL conformance baseline for already-corrected canonical onboarding queries.
